bullets.title: May Retail Sales Beat Broadly; 2Q Real Consumption Tracking Lifted to 2.9%
bullets.body: May headline retail sales came in at +0.9% m/m (consensus +0.6%), with control group +0.7% vs. +0.4% expected; YoY retail sales +6.9% vs. April's +4.8%. Morgan Stanley raised 2Q real consumption tracking 0.7pt to 2.9% q/q on the strength, with goods spending running +4.6%. E-commerce +1.47% MoM and sporting goods +10.8% YoY were standouts; restaurant sales were a drag.

bullets.title: FOMC Today: Dots Move to Zero 2026 Cuts; Warsh Press Conference Is the Main Event
bullets.body: Consensus expects the Fed to remove easing bias, shift median dot from 1 cut to 0 cuts with the rate holding at 3.625% (a 3.875% median would be market-negative). Warsh is expected to withhold his own dot and may signal a regime shift away from forward guidance, increasing scope for rate volatility. A dovish comment on tariff/energy pass-through effects in the press conference would be the upside catalyst for risk assets.

bullets.title: Sector Rotation: Mega-Cap Funding Semis, Financials, Industrials; Momentum Intact
bullets.body: Market color shows mega-cap names are the source of funds flowing into semiconductors, financials, and industrials; 12-month winners are up ~2% despite mega-cap weakness. Broader market breadth is positive with 65%+ of S&P 500 names higher YTD even as Info Tech and Comm Services weigh on SPX in June (Financials +5%, Industrials +4%). S&P 500 flat at ~7,512 with VIX at 16.87 (+2.8%).

bullets.title: Semis Rally 2.7%+ Pre-Market; SOXX +2.67% on AI Demand and Korea Strength
bullets.body: Semiconductors broadly higher pre-market led by INTC +3.6% (18A process milestone at VLSI Symposium), AMAT +3.8% (EssilorLuxottica JDA), CRDO +3.0%, ALAB +2.8%, and MU/WDC on Korea overnight strength. UBS adds Lam Research to Most Preferred, removes Snowflake; maintains NVDA as top semiconductor pick. Semi cap equipment makers reportedly raising prices 5-10%, providing WFE upside mainly in 2027.

bullets.title: AVGO: JPM High Conviction; 5-Year GOOGL TPU Agreement Through v11, 2027 AI Revenue 2-2.5x
bullets.body: JPM's Harlan Sur defending AVGO: TPU v8i 3nm 'Sunfish' fully qualified and ramping with 18+ month lead over Google's MediaTek alternative; TPU v9 2nm on-track for C28 with no delays. A 5-year GOOGL/AVGO agreement through TPU v11 with annual revenue commitment increases through 2031 is in place. Wolfe notes AVGO's $29bn XPV residual value backstop is a risk but if financing closes, 20-25GW FY28 capacity implies $250-300bn XPU revenue potential.

bullets.title: AI Capex Financing: Hyperscaler Debt Issuance Accelerating; $300B Since November
bullets.body: Top 4 US hyperscalers face ~$700-725bn capex in 2026 (+75% YoY); GOOGL consuming essentially all internal cash by FY27/28, META faces ~$100bn cumulative funding gap, MSFT ~$90-130bn gaps FY27-28. $300bn of AI/data center debt has been issued since November alone; IG debt expected to do heavy lifting (~$2.1tn over 2026-30). USD share of issuance has dropped to ~63% from 86% last year as supply globalizes. Data center financing reached $58B YTD vs. $34B at this point last year.

bullets.title: MSFT Copilot Cowork GA: Usage-Based Pricing, Multi-Model Strategy, 30-40% Cheaper Than Claude
bullets.body: Microsoft launched Copilot Cowork globally with task-based Copilot Credits pricing, emphasizing cost and governance as differentiators over pure performance. Multi-model strategy spans Anthropic Opus/Sonnet, OpenAI GPT-5.5, and in-house Cowork 1; internal testing shows 30-40% cost reduction vs. Anthropic Claude. MSFT is also considering a hosted DeepSeek version for further cost savings; a $3B+ MSFT-ORCL infrastructure deal reportedly fell through on security/compliance concerns.

bullets.title: Grid/Power Infrastructure: FERC Vote Tomorrow Could Unlock IPP Contracting; TLN Outperforming
bullets.body: FERC meeting tomorrow addresses data center interconnection process and co-location tariffs, needed for PJM to resume data center contracting; IPP positioning is at its lowest since the 'Powering AI' trade began. Transformer lead times average 128-144 weeks (vs. 12-16 pre-COVID) and US grid interconnection backlog exceeds 2x installed capacity. Bernstein initiated CEG and VST outperform, GEV outperform at $1,206 TP, while downgrading FSLR to underperform on 45X tax credit policy dependency.

bullets.title: SNAP Specs Disappoint at $2,195; AR Glasses Remain Functionally Immature
bullets.body: SNAP unveiled Specs AR glasses at $2,195 with 4-hour battery life and a bulky form factor, widely panned vs. META Ray-Bans at $224-$799. Multiple sources view the competitive entry as TAM expansion rather than share loss, noting the technology remains far from a functional all-day form factor. AMAT is partnering with EssilorLuxottica on AR/AI glasses optics combining photonics waveguide technology.

bullets.title: UK CPI Slows to 2.8% but Services Jump to 3.7%; BoE Expected to Hold Tomorrow
bullets.body: UK May headline CPI rose 0.2% m/m / 2.8% y/y, below expectations, but services CPI surged to 3.7% from 3.2% — the BoE's most-watched measure. One model shows upside inflation risk consistent with 4.3% CPI by December vs. 3.6% consensus; GDP growth tracking just 0.5% y/y in 3Q26. Markets are pricing one hike to 4.0% by year-end; FTSE is off -4% from late-February highs and underperforming the S&P 500.

bullets.title: Gold: Extreme One-Sided Positioning Creates Tactical Upside Setup
bullets.body: Gold is up ~25% since March pullback lows, but GS data shows GLD call skew at decade lows and put skew at record highs — extreme one-sided bearish positioning that may provide a tactical catalyst to the upside. Sentiment had been very negative following early-year meme-driven volatility.

bullets.title: 30-Year UST Joins UK Gilt as Bearish Trend Signal; Long Duration via BNDD
bullets.body: Hedgeye notes the US 30-year yield has joined the UK 10-year Gilt in a bearish trend signal, interpreting rates moving lower as confirming the inflation cycle peak is in the rear-view; CRB index is down 11% from its peak. Gas prices fell below $4 for the first time since April on Iran peace deal news, and crude oil WTI declined 16% over the prior week.

bullets.title: May Pending Home Sales +3.8% M/M, 7-Month High — Housing Recovery Continues Despite Rates
bullets.body: May pending home sales surged +3.8% m/m vs. consensus +0.9%, reaching a 7-month high and now up +2.1% y/y. The gain came despite mortgage rates climbing ~50bps over the past 15 weeks. However, weekly mortgage applications retreated 3.8% w/w, with purchases down 3.4% and refis down 4.5%, suggesting some near-term friction.

bullets.title: Euro Area Inflation Remains Elevated; Core to Stay Near 2.5% Through Year-End
bullets.body: JPMorgan forecasts Euro area headline HICP to rise from 2.0% in 1Q26 to 3.0% in 2Q-4Q26, with core staying at 2.4-2.6% through 2026 driven by sticky services inflation at 3.0-3.5%. Core inflation 3-month momentum is running at 3.2% annualized, reflecting stronger pre-conflict pricing pressure; technology price drag has plateaued with no further disinflationary benefit expected.

bullets.title: CRM Hits 52-Week Low After 11 Consecutive Down Days; Software Broadly Weak
bullets.body: CRM is down 11 straight trading days — its longest-ever streak — back to late-2018 levels with minimal analyst engagement. IGV is down ~15% in June, with SNOW, CRWD, and MDB off mid-teens in 2 weeks; Technology Services leads all sectors in new 52-week lows. UBS moved CRM, INTU, and PANW from Most Preferred to Bellwether and took a cautious stance on software despite 'attractive current valuations.'

bullets.title: Warsh Fed Communication Shift: Less Forward Guidance Is Minor; Policy Accuracy Matters More
bullets.body: A note argues the Fed's historical failures (Depression, 1970s inflation, GFC, Covid) stem from policy errors, not communication gaps, and that Warsh's preference for limited rate guidance is a minor benefit. More important is whether the Fed is correct on inflation; the trimmed mean metric debate is a distraction. The note calls out Fed 'noble lies' since the GFC as a trust-undermining practice.

bullets.title: China Food Delivery Regulation Tightens; PDD Faces ~CNY1.5B Fine
bullets.body: China's SAMR is proposing to ban long-term, large-scale platform subsidies that restrict competition and will require transparent subsidy disclosure. PDD Holdings faces the largest individual fine of ~CNY1.5B ($219M) among e-tailers from April 2026 actions; seven food delivery platforms were collectively fined CNY3.60B in April for safety violations.

bullets.title: OPEX Tomorrow Is Call-Heavy; SpotGamma: Long Above 7,500, Short Below
bullets.body: Tomorrow's options expiration is described as call-heavy, suggesting volatility potential next week as positions roll off. SpotGamma framework: long stocks while SPX > 7,500, short below. An Iran deal signed before OPEX is cited as a potential additional positive catalyst for the grind higher.

bullets.title: Convertible Bond Issuance at Highest Level Since COVID; Luxury EU Record Call Buying
bullets.body: Citi flags convertible bond issuance at its highest level since COVID. EU Luxury is seeing record call option buying averaging $670M/day with a single-day record of $1.5B. These cross-asset signals suggest risk appetite remains elevated in pockets despite mega-cap softness.

bullets.title: Restaurant Sector: Check Growth Stalled Since Dec 2025; No Longer Supporting Sales
bullets.body: Citi notes that average check growth, which was a consistent positive contributor to restaurant sector sales from mid-2023 through late 2025, came under pressure starting December 2025. Into 2026, transaction growth is no longer fueling sector-level sales, marking a meaningful regime change for restaurant operators.
